title: High Resolution 3D Imaging of Ex-Vivo Biological Samples by Micro CT
protocol: Remove post mortem leg from a C57/Bl6 embryo at 18.5 days post-conception.
Seal one narrow end of a polystyrene pipette tip (20-200 μl) using epoxy resin or another glue.
Fill the sealed pipette tip with working buffer (PBS or other).
Fit the leg tightly into the filled pipette tip and seal the other end with parafilm sheet.
Place the prepared pipette tip into a suitable holder for imaging.
Set the instrument to 40 KV and 200 μA for imaging the mouse femur embryo.
Acquire 1000 projection images at 4x magnification for an 8μ resolution.
Orthotopically implant non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) NCI-H460 into nude rat lungs.
Wait until lung cancer nodules become detectable, approximately 4 weeks after implantation.
Sacrifice the rat immediately and infuse it with a saline solution mixed with heparin.
Inject the rat with a diluted Microfil solution (2 ml compound solution, 3 ml diluent, 0.3 ml curing agent) into the left ventricle to stain the bronchial circulation.
Extract the lungs and heart of the rat.
Immobilize the extracted sample tightly into a 50 ml plastic test tube.
Damp a cloth in ethanol and place it at the bottom of the tube to create a saturated ethanol atmosphere.
Glue or screw the tube containing the sample into a holder of the instrument.
Set the imaging parameters for complete lung imaging: source set at 40KV and 100 μA, acquire 2500 projection images at a magnification of 0.5x to achieve 16μ resolution.
Place the sample in the rotation stage of the instrument.
Take an initial x-ray image with arbitrarily set voltage and current.
Increase the number of photons by slightly increasing the current if the image is too dark.
If necessary, further increase the brightness by raising the voltage on the x-ray tube.
Decrease the voltage first, then reduce the current if the image is too bright.
Improve image brightness using binning; set to 2 for a 4 times brighter but half-resolution image compared to binning of 1.
Optimize exposure time after setting optimum brightness to balance contrast and experiment duration.
Enhance contrast for low-absorbing samples by using filters that reduce lower energy photon flux.
Choose the working magnification from options: 0.5x, 4x, 10x, 20x, or 40x.
Adjust distances between x-ray source and sample to get optimal resolution and field of view.
Increase distance between x-ray source and sample for better resolution but smaller field of view.
Decrease the distance from sample to detector to increase field of view and reduce resolution.
Take an image at 0 degrees.
Rotate the sample to -20 degrees.
Reposition the sample if the desired volume has shifted laterally.
Continue rotating the sample and correcting its position until the field of interest is inside the image from -90 to 90 degrees.
Take projection images between -90 and 90 degrees.
Proceed to reconstruct the sample volume after obtaining the required projection images.
Calibrate the image scale using a standard phantom under the same experimental conditions as for the sample.
Recalibrate the sample image using the values obtained from the phantom.
Use linear interpolation or extrapolation to adjust pixel values based on set limits for water and bone.
Select an image analysis software designed to handle large files up to 20GB.
